integration.r3_fix: First full-scale Windows panoramic run (2026-08-01, 8782 files) ended ROUND_REVIEW_REQUIRED_RED_ERRORS_REMAIN with the RED count oscillating 20-21 across rounds and 483 Hydra / 1640 SSOT groups. Root cause: the inventory walked the engine's own runtime root (supportive modules/.../v0162B/runtime), re-analyzing prior runs' sandbox copies, evidence files and the truncated corpses left by the earlier [Errno 28] disk-full crash - RED errors no sandbox repair can converge, plus duplicate-basename Hydra/SSOT noise. R3 excludes the engine's own runtime root (run_dir parent) from inventory. Companion: qa/via_red_triage_v001.py + VIA.ps1 -Do Report distill any run (including pre-R3 runs) into a paste-sized RED triage Markdown. Verified live: a base seeded with a corrupt old run_* directory (invalid JSON + Python syntax error + duplicate engine basename) gates UNIFIED_SANDBOX_GREEN with zero runtime-polluted inventory rows. Both daily entrypoints re-locked to the R3 launcher SHA.
integration.note: The original 143477-byte AllInOne (sha256 e6155465203591fd34d800a0901099bddf537f2aae04277281a752e2aff48127) was not present in the supplied artifact set. It was reconstructed from the byte-verified audit engine and UI preview using the v0162B repair contract (single-quoted literal here-strings only, placeholder-replacement daily-launcher template, post-generation AST validation, exact-SHA asset verification). Both daily entrypoints were re-locked to the reconstructed launcher's SHA-256.
integration.r2_fix: First Windows runtime user test (2026-07-28 15:34, py 3.13.7) exposed an argument-quoting defect: Start-Process joined array arguments without quoting, so the engine path containing spaces ('supportive modules') was split and Python failed with Errno 2. R2 quotes every whitespace-containing argument explicitly and passes one command line. Both daily entrypoints re-locked to the R2 launcher SHA.
